title: Longitudinal modes of a 30 cm HeNe cavity
caption: Standing waves fit the cavity when f = qc/2L, spaced by Δf = c/2L = 500 MHz for L = 30 cm. Under a gain curve 1.5 GHz wide, three modes (centre and ±500 MHz) lie above half gain; the next ones, ±1000 MHz, fall outside it. Real lasers use the modes that reach threshold.
alt: Graph of gain against frequency from -1100 to 1100 megahertz: a bell-shaped gain curve 1500 megahertz wide with three vertical lines at -500, 0 and 500 megahertz marking the cavity modes.
description: The horizontal axis is frequency relative to the centre of the gain curve in megahertz; the vertical axis is the relative gain.
The bell curve is the gain, 1.5 GHz wide at half maximum (it is 0.5 at ±750 MHz).
The cavity modes are the vertical lines, spaced by c/2L = 3 × 10⁸/0.6 = 500 MHz: at −500, 0 and +500 MHz.
About 3 modes fit within the gain bandwidth.
